identity: A page of controls where the user must find and use the control named in the instruction.

scenarios.name: button
scenarios.screen: The page shows clickable controls with distinct labels, sometimes alongside sentences or labeled text fields. A typical set has several buttons, and some labels can be similar or appear on disabled controls.
never: A button already pressed in a sequence.
A menu or dialog open over the buttons.
An Undo control before a choice is made.

arrangements.text: Several labeled controls sit among short text and fields in the main task area.
A row of similar controls runs across the top of a compact task area.
Similar controls sit together inside a card.
Similar controls run along the bottom of the task area.

scenarios.hint: Show the exact requested button label, or a single obvious button when no label is specified. Do not substitute a link.

scenarios.name: sequence
scenarios.screen: Two to four labeled buttons are scattered across the task area. None has been pressed yet.
never: A completed press shown on load.
A popup containing the next button.
More than four sequence buttons.

arrangements.text: The buttons occupy separated positions across the task area.
The buttons form two loose rows with space between their positions.

scenarios.hint: Show all named buttons in a scrambled spatial arrangement; task specifies sequence, none has been clicked.

scenarios.name: link
scenarios.screen: Paragraphs contain inline links among ordinary words, or a related-items list contains links presented as text, buttons, or chips. All links are visible at the start.
never: A link preview already open.
A tab hiding the target link.
A Back control before a link is followed.

arrangements.text: Paragraphs stack vertically, with links embedded in their lines.
A related-items list sits beneath its heading, with one linked item per row.

scenarios.hint: Show the exact target word as an underlined link embedded among other readable text and links.

scenarios.name: tab
scenarios.screen: A strip of tabs sits above one visible content panel. In tab selection tasks the target tab starts inactive; in link tasks, only the active tab's text and links are visible.
scenarios.scene: In link tasks, the tab containing the target link is active and its content is visible.
never: Every tab panel visible at once.
A link from an inactive tab floating outside its panel.
The target tab already active in a tab selection task.

arrangements.text: Tab headers run horizontally above the active panel's text.
Tab headers stack beside the active panel's text.

scenarios.hint: Show tabs including the requested number or one open tab containing the requested exact link. Link and tab labels must be readable.

scenarios.name: menu
scenarios.screen: The task shows either a visible menu of people or a Menu button with its app menu closed. Nested submenu choices are closed at the normal start.
scenarios.scene: The menu is open through every submenu on the target path, with the target item visible and unselected; the button version also has its main panel open.
never: A target menu item already selected.
All nested submenus open at once.
The button version's menu panel open at the normal start.

arrangements.text: People's names sit in a menu bar across the task area.
A Menu button sits above the area where its menu panel opens.

scenarios.name: collapsible
scenarios.screen: A vertical list of section headers is visible, with their contents collapsed. In link tasks, the links are inside those hidden sections.
scenarios.scene: In link tasks, the target's section is open and its link is visible. In section expansion tasks, a different section is open while the target remains closed.
never: Every section expanded on load.
A link from a closed section visible outside it.
The target section already open in a section expansion task.

arrangements.text: Section headers stack vertically, and an open section's content sits directly below its header.
Section headers occupy a narrow column, with each open section's content aligned beside its header.

scenarios.hint: Show section headers with expansion affordances. Required section or link must exist; for numbered section 44 use an internally scrolled panel with that header visible.

scenarios.name: dialog
scenarios.screen: A dialog shows a title, body text, a close button, and zero, two, or three action buttons. In opener cases, a page button is visible and the dialog starts closed.
scenarios.scene: The dialog is open with its close button and any action buttons visible, including in opener cases.
never: Four or more dialog action buttons.
Two dialogs stacked together.
A dialog already dismissed on load.

arrangements.text: The dialog title sits above its text, with the close button at the top edge and action buttons below the text.
A page button sits above the area occupied by the dialog after it opens.

scenarios.name: pie
scenarios.screen: The page has a place to open a radial menu; its labeled slices are closed at the normal start.
scenarios.scene: The radial menu is expanded, showing its labeled slices around the center with none selected.
never: Pie slices already visible at the normal start.
A slice already selected.
A separate list of pie items beside the closed menu.

arrangements.text: The menu's opening spot sits near the center of the task area.
The menu's opening spot sits off center with room around it for the slices.

scenarios.hint: Show an expanded radial pie menu with the requested letter in one clearly clickable sector and other letters around it.

scenarios.name: widget
scenarios.screen: Five visible controls include a radio button, checkbox, single-line text field, multi-line text box, and button. The task asks for a click on one control type.
never: A widget type picker open on load.
Text already entered as the result of this task.
A hidden control that must be revealed.

arrangements.text: The five controls stack vertically with their associated text beside them.
The controls occupy two columns, with text fields on one side and selection controls on the other.

scenarios.hint: Show a small collection of actual widget types with visibly recognizable shapes: button, text entry, radio, checkbox and link. Target type is unambiguous.

scenarios.name: focus
scenarios.screen: Several labeled text fields are visible. No target field has been focused by the task yet, and the fields do not require typing.
never: A keyboard open over the fields.
Typed task text in the target field.
A field selection menu.

arrangements.text: Labeled fields stack vertically in top-to-bottom order.
Each label sits to the left of its field in a vertical form.

scenarios.hint: Show enough input textboxes for the requested ordinal, aligned in unambiguous reading order. No target focus ring yet.

scenarios.name: hover
scenarios.screen: Several squares occupy fixed positions in the task area. One square is highlighted, and the pointer has not yet accumulated hover time on it.
never: A completed hover timer on load.
A popup opened by the highlighted square.
The squares outside the task area.

arrangements.text: Squares sit at separated positions across the task area.
Squares occupy separated positions in two loose rows.

scenarios.hint: Show one blue square, pointer outside it, a dwell counter below the requested total, and a clear movement area. Movement is explained in notes, not multiple duplicate squares.

scenarios.name: tooltip-inspect
scenarios.screen: An icon task shows several icon-only toolbar buttons; an ID task shows rows of names with action buttons. No tooltip is showing at the normal start.
never: Every tooltip visible at once.
A target tooltip already open on load.
The icon task's button names printed beside all icons.

arrangements.text: Icon-only buttons run in a toolbar across the task area.
Names form a vertical list, with each row's action button to the right.

scenarios.name: rows
scenarios.screen: A table lists people or files in labeled columns. Each row has actions that appear when that row is hovered; no row actions are showing at the normal start.
never: Every row's actions visible on load.
An overflow menu for a row.
A row already removed or archived.

arrangements.text: Column headings sit above a vertical stack of rows, with names at the left and other cells to the right.
File names sit in the first column, followed by other file details across each row.

scenarios.name: context
scenarios.screen: Files appear in a browser as a grid or list. No context menu is open and no file has been right-clicked at the normal start.
never: A context menu open on load.
A context menu detached from its file.
The target action already applied.

arrangements.text: Files occupy cells in a grid across the task area.
Files stack in rows with their details aligned in columns.

scenarios.name: open
scenarios.screen: A file browser shows files in a grid or list. Files start unopened; toolbar-route tasks also show an Open button for the selected file.
never: The target file already open.
A file preview covering the browser.
A context menu open over a file.

arrangements.text: Files occupy cells in a grid.
Files stack in rows with names and details aligned.
An Open button sits in a toolbar above the files.

scenarios.name: hover-menu
scenarios.screen: Top-level navigation entries are visible in the page header. Their grouped link dropdowns are closed until an entry is hovered.
never: A dropdown open at the normal start.
Every navigation group visible at once.
A target link shown outside its dropdown.

arrangements.text: Top-level entries run horizontally, with each dropdown positioned beneath its entry when open.
Top-level entries occupy one side of the header, with the opened group extending inward below them.

scenarios.name: flyout
scenarios.screen: A department-menu trigger is visible. The department list and its nested category panels are closed at the normal start.
never: All submenu levels open on load.
A category panel visible without its department list.
A target already selected.

arrangements.text: The trigger sits at the left of the task area, where successive menu panels extend to the right.
The trigger sits higher in the task area, with the department list below it and deeper panels extending right.

scenarios.name: row-reveal
scenarios.screen: A table lists people or files. Each row's quick actions and overflow button appear only on row hover, and no overflow menu is open at the normal start.
never: Quick actions visible on every row at load.
An overflow menu already open.
A target action already applied.

arrangements.text: Rows stack below column headings, with each row's name at the left and its other cells to the right.
File rows place the file name in the first column and file details in columns beside it.
